lexicalLimitations: Negation lookbehind windows are bounded to 35-60 characters within a single clause/sentence delimited by [.;\n] (treating dots before word characters like Thread.sleep or Dispatchers.IO as identifier dots, not sentence boundaries); negation matching for these guards also stops at contrasting coordinators but/however/yet. Negations separated by longer clauses or across sentence boundaries fall outside the guard.
Double-negation phrasing (for example 'Do not forget to call Thread.sleep(500)') can evade a simple negation lookbehind and is not parsed syntactically.

Because scorer.ts compiles regex assertions case-insensitively ('i' flag), injected lowercase code such as withContext(dispatchers.io) cannot be lexically distinguished from hardcoded withContext(Dispatchers.IO); negative concurrency guards therefore target prose hardcoding/direct-call recommendations and ignoring injected properties, while un-negated anti-pattern snippets across newlines remain outside lexical regex scope.
Regex patterns accept stated domain terms and common paraphrases rather than arbitrary unseen synonyms or Kotlin AST dataflow.

controls.transcript: Places business logic in a UseCase in the Domain layer (pure Kotlin, no Android deps). ViewModel orchestrates, Repository handles data access only.

Put the pricing calculation in a domain-layer use case implemented in plain Kotlin, independent of Android APIs. It computes the order total from the supplied order data. The ViewModel calls that operation and maps its result to screen state; the repository only retrieves and persists the data needed by the operation.

Do not put business logic in the ViewModel or Repository. Implement order-total calculation in a pure Kotlin use case inside the domain layer with no Android dependencies; the ViewModel orchestrates UI state and the Repository handles data access.
